title: applied-ml-weekly-notes-2026-04-21
content:
Applied ML weekly research notes - week of 2026-04-21

Attendees (weekly sync / standups): Alyssa Chen (notes), Marco Silva, Priya Reddy, Omar Haddad, Lina Park (PM), Daniel Ortiz (infra)

TL;DR:
- Quantization experiments: 4-bit QLoRA-ish flows show promising latency/cost gains on A100s; accuracy regressions limited to ~0.6-1.2% for our eval set on instruction-following tasks when using mixed-per-channel quantization + bias correction.
- Evals: New benchmark (rm-commons-30) added; early regression detected on SummarizeLong for model v2.1 -> v2.2. Running targeted promptset to triage.
- Model onboarding: Internal checklist updated (inference-config + kernel hints). Onboarding of open-model-x-2.2 in progress; expected canary next Tue.

Notes / details:
1) Quantization experiments (Alyssa + Marco)
- Setup: baseline fp16 runs vs int4 (GPTQ-like) and hybrid int4+fp16 KV cache. Tests run on dedicated A100-80GB nodes, batch size distribution mirroring prod (p95 seq_len ~512).
- Findings:
  * Mixed per-channel int4 with symmetric clipping + per-tensor scaling reduces perplexity drift vs naive int4.
  * Adding bias-correction on linear layers recovers ~0.3-0.5% of the eval metric we lost otherwise.
  * Latency: median token latency improved 18-26% (depending on sequence length and batch). Cost per token estimated to drop ~32% under current infra pricing.
  * Failure modes: generation incoherence in long-context (>2k tokens) for some prompts - likely from KV cache precision loss; observed at low frequency (~0.6% of prompts).
- Next actions:
  * Marco: run longer-context KV-cache stress tests (10k tokens) and collect examples (JIRA-ML-3147). Due: 2026-04-28.
  * Alyssa: replicate top-10 failing prompts on CPU fp16 to rule out tokenizer or decoding-schedule issues. Due: 2026-04-23.

2) Evals / regression detection (Priya)
- New benchmark bundle: rm-commons-30 added to nightly eval harness; covers summarization, instruction-following, reasoning. First nightly run flagged a regression on SummarizeLong when upgrading from model v2.1 -> v2.2 (delta -4.3 ROUGE-L).
- Quick triage plan:
  * Run ablation on v2.2 with/without adapter layers (to check whether small fine-tune step caused shift).
  * Run evaluation with exact seed/call ordering to reproduce.
  * If reproduced, create a reduced promptset (20 examples) to run human eval and confirm perceptual quality.
- Action items:
  * Priya: produce reduced promptset and human-eval instructions. Due: 2026-04-24.
  * Omar: instrument console dashboard to surface per-route eval deltas and severity. Due: 2026-05-05.

3) Model onboarding (Omar + Lina)
- Checklist updates: added explicit fields for kernel hints, quantization-friendly model flags, and expected seq_len perf numbers. New onboarding doc: github.com/redwood-inference/model-onboarding/pull/62
- Open-model-x-2.2 onboarding status:
  * Artifacts: model weights + manifest received; conversion scripts ran (FP16->channels first layout).
  * Kernels: preliminary kernel hint suggests using fused attention kernel v3 for better memory locality.
  * Canary plan: 5% traffic on hosted API, two-day window, automatic rollback on eval/failure thresholds.
- Blockers:
  * Platform autoscaler currently rejects small instance types when telemetry shows high token-per-second bursts - infra team investigating.
  * Need a quantized-compat check in CI for PRs (currently manual).
- Next steps:
  * Omar: finalize canary rollout plan and create route in Console. Due: 2026-04-27.
  * Lina: align release notes and customer-impact statement. Due: 2026-04-26.

4) Infrastructure notes (Daniel)
- KV cache persistence experiments: writing warmed prefixes to local NVMe improved cold-start latency by ~200ms for popular prompts. Need to validate storage costs vs benefits.
- Autoscaler tuning: suggested policy tweak to prefer GPU pools with higher batching efficiency for spiky workloads. Daniel to propose config.

5) Risks / blockers
- Quantized long-context regressions need root cause before rolling out quantized kernels to Dedicated customers.
- Nightly eval pipeline currently doesn't snapshot FullCallTrace which complicates repro for stochastic failures.

6) Misc / open questions
- Should we include an explicit "quantization quality" label in model catalog entries (e.g., int8_ok, int4_experimental)? Proposal: yes, visible to users and helps routing policies. (Proposed by Alyssa)
- Proposal to add an automated reduced-eval step in CI that runs 50 short prompts for every model PR. Cost estimate needed. (Action: Priya to estimate by 2026-04-29)

Action item summary (owners/dates):
- Marco: KV-cache long-context stress tests and example collection (JIRA-ML-3147) - 2026-04-28
- Alyssa: replicate failing prompts on fp16 CPU - 2026-04-23
- Priya: reduced promptset + human-eval instructions for SummarizeLong regression - 2026-04-24
- Omar: canary rollout plan + Console route for open-model-x-2.2 - 2026-04-27
- Lina: release notes / customer impact - 2026-04-26
- Daniel: autoscaler config proposal - 2026-04-30
- Priya: CI reduced-eval cost estimate - 2026-04-29

Notes to self / informal:
- Keep a stash of top 50 failing prompts (internal bucket) for triage - saves time on human eval repro.
- Consider short A/B with quantized vs fp16 on low-risk beta accounts before wider Dedicated rollout.

References / links: Confluence page CONFLUENCE-ML-4982 for quantization playbook; JIRA-ML-3147 for KV-cache failures; PR: github.com/redwood-inference/model-onboarding/pull/62

End of notes.
